title: Optimality of the row best response
statement: Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with a nonempty set of $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ with $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$, and let $q$ be a mixed strategy for the column player. For a pure row $i$, write $u(i) = \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j$ for its expected payoff against $q$, and let $i^\ast$ be a row maximising $u$. Then $u(i) \le u(i^\ast)$ for every row $i$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite zero-sum game with M rows and N columns
the row action set is nonempty (M ≠ 0)
q is a mixed column strategy
i^* is the maximiser of the expected pure-row payoff against q
i is an arbitrary pure row
replaced:
For any game $G$, mixed column strategy $q$, and pure row $i$,
\[
  \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G, i, q)
  \;\le\;
  \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G, \mathrm{bestRow}(G, q), q).
\]
